ops.statement: internal/refusal exports TildeDir, TildeFile and TildeEntry — go-dt's ToTilde with OrFullPath that returns the full path when $HOME is unknown — because dt.ToTilde panics unless EnsureUserHomeDir succeeded, and every typed caller needs that guard; refusal.EnsureHome is the one call that resolves $HOME
just test-go also runs the tests under cmd/, so TestInitialize and the temp-HOME binary test run with the suite; just lint runs the pathlint whole-tree check alone
golang.org/x/tools becomes a direct dependency at v0.52.0 (go/packages, go/analysis) because v0.48.0 cannot read Go 1.27 export data; x/mod and x/sync move with it

entries.note: main calls refusal.EnsureHome(), which is dt.EnsureUserHomeDir() plus a record of whether it succeeded (P22). A failure is not a refusal: the command runs, and every conversion returns the full path. TestPathsShowTildeUnderHome runs settings migrate with HOME unset and sees the full path.

refusal.Tilde: $HOME/ is replaced wherever it appears; a bare $HOME only when bounded exactly as the analysis lists. Table-driven test covers /Users/mikey, /Users/mike.old, cwd=/Users/mike, (in /Users/mike), quotes, backticks, a sentence-ending period, and no-HOME.
Render applies Tilde to the person text and to the agent body; Verdict applies it to the verdict line, so the bracketing lines show ~ too. TestRenderShowsTilde covers person, agent and verdict.

errorscmd: show's Summary line, printDetails' Detail and every Fields value, printLogOnly's summary and DB error, the listing's SUMMARY column; faultrow.restText. The detail-log path printLogOnly prints goes through refusal.TildeFile.

The printed-path rule reports none over internal/ and cmd/. Converted sites: settings migrate's three prints (dt.Filepath), verify's CTRF line (dt.Filepath), errors list's detail-log path. Each uses refusal.TildeFile/TildeDir, which is go-dt's ToTilde with OrFullPath behind the no-HOME guard (P22).

Converted: hookcmd SessionStart Detail (cwd) and hook fault 'binary'; liveview restart 'path'/'resolved'; monitor schema refusal 'db'/'binary', worktree_unsettled 'worktree' (x2), unlanded_cache 'cache_dir', unlanded_refresh Summary and 'project_root', reap 'worktree'; mainsyncjob Detail 'In <root>' and 'root' (x2). Fingerprints are untouched.

tildePath, monitor.displayPath and verifycmd.displayPath are gone with their tests; callers use refusal.TildeDir/TildeEntry on dt types. Nothing prints cwd-relative any more. A verify.toml check greps that neither helper exists.

internal/pathlint.Analyzer: fmt.Print/Println/Printf, and Fprint/Fprintln/Fprintf whose writer is os.Stdout or os.Stderr, with an argument typed dt.DirPath, dt.Filepath or dt.EntryPath. A Tilde* type passes, which is how both go-dt's ToTilde and the refusal wrappers satisfy it. Fixture test with want-comments.
All eight calls, each diagnostic naming the go-dt replacement; test files exempt (a fixture path is never shown to anyone). Fixture test covers every call plus filepath.Clean as a non-match.

internal/pathlint/baseline.txt: 160 lines of '<file> <enclosing function>' covering 269 calls (66 in internal/monitor). Embedded into the analyzer; TestBaselineNamesOnlyLiveSites fails on a line no site matched, and the baseline-hit set is the analyzer's result so the whole-tree run can compute it.

TestRepoHasNoNewFindings loads ./internal/... and ./cmd/... with go/packages (export data for deps, so under a second) and runs the analyzer; `just lint` runs that test and the baseline test alone. Driven by a small loader rather than go/analysis/checker, which would type-check every dependency from source.

cmd/endless-go/tilde_test.go builds the binary and runs it under a resolved temp HOME: settings list over a legacy boolean as a person and as an agent (ENDLESS_AUDIENCE=agent), settings migrate, settings migrate FILE (the converted direct print), errors list/show/show --detail of a recorded fault with a path, the log-only listing with its detail-log path, and HOME unset. Each fails on $HOME/ in the output.
tilde() returns ~ for home itself and ~/… for home + os.sep; anything else unchanged. Two tests added to tests/test_config.py.
No JSON output, written file or child-process argument changed. The detail log's format is unchanged; its Fields values carry the ~ form P7 stores, which is the plan's intent.
--report-dir and the sandbox directory are still printed absolute; neither site was touched.
The 160 baselined sites are untouched; the baseline only shrinks from here.
go-dt is unchanged. The no-HOME guard the plan did not foresee lives in internal/refusal (P22), not in go-dt.
homeRelative and the stored projects.path form are untouched.

writeTargetRedirect, bashWritesRefusal, cdRedirect (the /cd line included) and unboundWorktreeInstruction show every path with ~. New hookcmd/tilde_paths_test.go plus the flipped TestCdRedirect assert ~/ and no $HOME/.

Not in the plan: dt.ToTilde panics via dt.GetUserHomeDir when EnsureUserHomeDir never succeeded, so P1's 'paths print in full' needs a guard at every typed conversion. Three one-line wrappers in refusal (the package that already owns display) carry it; the analyzer accepts their Tilde* results like go-dt's own.
cmd/endless-go and cmd/endless-migrate already had tests that just test-go never ran; the P13 test lives beside them, so the recipe now covers ./cmd/... too.

go/packages at v0.48.0 fails with 'export data version 5 is greater than maximum supported version 4' under Go 1.27; v0.52.0 is the current release. Tidied from a copy at main's depth because go.mod's relative replaces do not resolve from the worktree.

entries.note: Update, insert and delete work on all 19 targets with --reason required (ED-1652). A delete marks the row removed = 1 on any table that has a removed column, tasks (ED-1547) and, since E-2010 landed and main was merged in, decisions, and deletes the row elsewhere; the task-only special case is gone. The command is now `endless correct <target> <update|insert|delete|annotate> [KEY]`, one positional argument (ED-1647), as the EQ-252 answer asked. The answer holds: the task as it stands is exactly what it chose, soft removal by column plus the subcommand shape, and nothing else in the task changed.
entries.holds_reason: The task now does exactly what the answer chose: soft removal on any table with a removed column (now proven on decisions too, after E-2010 landed), a hard delete elsewhere, and the target/operation/key command shape; nothing else in the task changed.

entries.note: RowChangedPayload{target, key, op, values}; an insert's values include the allocated id.
CorrectedPayload{reason, skip_gates, before[], refs[]}, written right after its change entry and committed with it in one ledger commit.
Writer.Append takes a flock on .endless/tmp/db-ledger.lock per append; BeginRun/EndRun hold it across a correction run. The lock dir gets its own .gitignore of *.
AppendOffset returns the segment size before the line (first line of a run) or the previous offset plus the previous line's length including its newline; a test checks each offset starts a line.
One applyRowChanged for executor and projector; ledger.corrected is a declared no-op in both. A test replays a ledger holding a correction and compares the row to the live one.

The annotation is its own subcommand, `endless correct <target> annotate KEY --reason`, since the EQ-252 answer made the operation a subcommand rather than the absence of a flag; it records ledger.corrected with refs = [] and no before, for a table target's existing row or for conversation, message and project_next (which take only annotate) with any id.
Python refuses before any subprocess (agent_env.present()), and endless-go correct refuses again from agentenv.Present(); both a REPORT.

Gates: the transition table for the task's type, the landed→assumed by-hand rule, plan-item approval for a status that reports work, the maybe-parent rule, and the vocabularies of task status/phase, session state, decision status, question status, plan item state/kind and project status. --skip-gates bypasses all of them and is recorded as skip_gates on the correction.
An unknown target names every target; an unlisted column names the target's allowed columns; both hold with --skip-gates.

A no-op --set is refused after comparing before values. A delete counts referrers through every declared foreign key plus the undeclared references (session_tasks, session_notices, hidden/pinned tasks, task_deps, decision_relations, session_statuses…); a task's own task_content rows do not count.

docsweep.RewriteMirrors rewrites and commits the mirrors of the task (content, items.toml) or decision touched; skipped in a sandbox. The run goes through dispatch, not dispatchWithNotices, and calls no derived emitter, so no notices, session rows or epic derivation.
A status correction on an epic (by current type or by the type set in the same run) adds the note; Python prints it under the summary.
Subject: `Endless: ledger.corrected E-NNNN <reason>`; the correction leads the subject even though its change entries precede it, and a commit holding a correction is never amended into or onto.

internal/events/correction_test.go, internal/correctcmd/correct_test.go, tests/test_correct_cmd.py: each operation, a plan item, concurrent appends, offsets, the agent refusal on both sides, gates with and without --skip-gates, annotations, projection parity, the commit subject and no-fold.
No audit command; git log is the only display.
